comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The first way gave this error

> Error: failed to register device: Post "https://<redacted-host>/auth/v1/register?device_id=rclone-44vt04llECptGXr3FwurU": read tcp 192.168.1.195:52037->185.179.129.36:443: wsarecv: En eksisterende forbindelse blev tvangsafbrudt af en ekstern vært.

Translated that means "An existing connection was forcibly terminated by a remote host."

```
$ curl "https://<redacted-host>/auth/v1/register?device_id=rclone-44vt04llECptGXr3FwurU"
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```

This looks like Jottacloud have firewalled this endpoint to stop people using it.

There is a bug in the No branch which is giving the `Reveal failed: input too short when revealing password - is it obscured` which can be fixed like this

```diff
--- a/backend/jottacloud/jottacloud.go
+++ b/backend/jottacloud/jottacloud.go
@@ -242,12 +242,12 @@ machines.`)
                authCode, _ := m.Get("auth_code")
 
                srv := rest.NewClient(fshttp.NewClient(ctx))
-               clientID, ok := m.Get(configClientID)
-               if !ok {
+               clientID, _ := m.Get(configClientID)
+               if clientID == "" {
                        clientID = legacyClientID
                }
-               clientSecret, ok := m.Get(configClientSecret)
-               if !ok {
+               clientSecret, _ := m.Get(configClientSecret)
+               if clientSecret == "" {
                        clientSecret = legacyEncryptedClientSecret
                }
 
```

But it ends up trying to access the same endpoint with exactly the same error

```
2025/09/25 11:30:11 NOTICE: Fatal error: failed to get oauth token: Post "https://<redacted-host>/auth/v1/token: ...: read: connection reset by peer
```

@participant3 @participant5 you've both worked on this bit of code - can you help?

comments.body:
> I'm not sure about that rclone authorize issue.

I looked into it some more, and I also found an old issue on this very same topic:
- https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/6496

This never worked - for the Telia, Tele2 and Onlime services that before this used the "whitelabel authentication", i.e. neither "standard" nor "legacy".

The reason it does not work is the customized configuration flow used in the Jottacloud backend. It can be made to work, but it requires some refactoring in this part of the implementation, and also probably changes to configuration where it would need to store the authentication type and whitelabel service type into the configuration (today these are only used during the configuration process to choose between the different authentication implementations, and deduce necessary information, where some of it may be stored in the configuration file, like a token URL and the token string). I don't want to do that now, and not as part of this pull request.

The web browser based authentication, which leads to the need for use of the rclone authorize command for headless machines, is only relevant for the whitelabel authentications, not standard (regular Jottacloud), nor legacy (currently none, but previously all the Elkjøp subsidiaries).

There is a workaround, mentioned previously in this issue:

> I was able to copy over the config so maybe that not something thats highly needed...

And in the older issue:

> I use another machine with a browser to authenticate rclone against Jotta Cloud, and finish creating the remote so it's saved as a config file then just copy the rclone config over to the headless machine.

To conclude:

I can add a note to the documentation about this limitation, and mention the workaround. Let me know if you do not agree with my statements above. When this is done, and the pull request is merged, this issue will be closed.

If you think this is something that should be fixed, then we create a separate issue for it. Or reopen #6496, which was closed as completed - I assume based on the fact that the workaround was acceptable by the reporter.

I reproduced the above issue. I used my regular Jottacloud account, but with the traditional web-based authentication that the whitelabels use (I've added support for regular Jottacloud with this as well in https://github.com/rclone/rclone/pull/8878, which is the source of the beta https://<redacted-host>/branch/jotta-auth-refactor I mentioned).

What I did:
- Created two remotes against my Jottacloud account.
- Observed in https://jottacloud.com/web/secure, under "My logged in devices", that there were one new entry - not two.
- Wait one hour, until the tokens expire.
- Run a request (e.g. rclone about) against one of the remotes: It refreshes the token successfully.
- Run a request against the other remote: It fails!
  > DEBUG : xremote: got fatal oauth error: oauth2: "invalid_grant" "Session doesn't have required client"
  > CRITICAL: Failed to create file system for "xremote:": couldn't get customer info: Get "https://<redacted-host>/account/v1/customer": couldn't fetch token: invalid_grant: maybe token expired? - try refreshing with "rclone config reconnect xremote:"

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I'm not too experienced with OAuth details... But based on the experience so far, these are my thoughts:

It seems to me the tokens you get for this traditional web-based authentication are tied to the machine. When you sign in with another session, it being configuring another rclone remote, or the official desktop application, you basically get the same token - or rather a refreshed version of that same token. And on token refresh, Jottacloud is known to refresh not only the access token but also the refresh token. Your existing sessions will have the old token, which works until it expires (1 hour), and when it tries to refresh it then it will then use its stored refresh token - which is now an old token and Jottacloud will not allow it. Jottacloud's token service responds HTTP 400 (BadRequest), with JSON data: {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Session doesn't have required client"}. The token will now be invalidated on server. The first session where you successfully refreshed the token, will also stop working eventually, after its token expire (1 hour) and it tries to refresh it again it will get the same "invalid_grant" error. So you have to re-authenticate, which gives you a completely new token.

With Personal Login Tokens this is a bit different, as each time you generate a new login token and trade it for a real (access+refresh) token, you are getting a unique token instance. Each of these can be refreshed individually, and revoked from the web GUI. There is a known case (documented in the backend docs) where copying the token would lead to problems: If you create one remote with personal login token, and then copy your rclone configuration to another machine and continue to use both remotes. You see, now you use the same token, and you end up with a similar case as above: One of them refreshes the token first, then when the other one tries to refresh the token it will use an outdated refresh token. As documented, we used to get "invalid_grant" errors in this case, but with description "Stale token". However, when I reproduce this case now I actually get the same description as we are experiencing with the traditional web-based authentication: "Session doesn't have required client". As before, the server has now invalidated the token, resulting in all uses of it (both rclone instances) continuously failing, and one had to create an entirely new token using a new personal login token.
